correctness.rationale: For every admissible Calderón–Lozanovskiĭ factorization, local Hölder gives the \(p_s\) estimate on each dyadic cube; the cube weight exponent is exactly the convex combination dictated by \(p_s\) and \(u_s\); outer Hölder with reciprocal exponent \(1/r_s\) then gives the Bourgain–Morrey norm inequality with constant one. The source verifies that the relevant lower generalized Boyd indices equal \(p_i\), so Theorem 1.9(i) applies under the stated \(q\) condition. All hypotheses and quantifiers are explicit, and no finite computation substitutes for an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The focal 2026 paper explicitly leaves its Bourgain–Morrey off-diagonal target abstract in the general parameter case. The accepted structural lemma gives a concrete Bourgain–Morrey envelope for every finite nontrivial pair of triples, so all of those new fractional estimates can be written in a standard named function space without compatibility assumptions. This is a motivated structural gap rather than an arbitrary parameter slice; it also cleanly separates what can be made explicit from the still-open reverse-inclusion/product-identification problem.
